sectionIntro: an inquiry into how people experience, interpret and make meaning through space. spanning architecture and environmental psychology, the work uses observation, qualitative research and design as tools to understand the relationships between built form, behaviour, identity and everyday experience.

items.title: interplay between place identity and affordances
items.description: an exploration into london's brick lane through the relationship between the physical environment, everyday activities and perceived place identity. qualitative research combined urban fieldwork and in-depth interviews to examine how spatial qualities shape what people perceive as possible within a place, and how those experiences contribute to their sense of belonging.
body: london's brick lane was studied as a place where spatial character, everyday activity, and cultural identity continually interact. the research asked how the physical qualities of an urban heritage environment support perceived possibilities for activity and perception, and how these experiences relate to the way people identify with the place.

the study used qualitative methods combining urban fieldwork with in-depth interviews and thematic analysis. observing the street as it was used, occupied, and navigated provided a spatial reading of the environment, while interviews brought forward how different users perceived and experienced those same conditions. the two were considered together to understand not only what the environment enables, but how those possibilities are interpreted by people with different relationships to the place.

the research positioned affordances and place identity as interconnected rather than separate aspects of environmental experience. the study found that brick lane's identity is sustained through a balance of change and continuity. its evolving landscape affords exploration, novelty and social interaction while traces of its past create familiarity, belonging and attachment. even amid gentrification and transformation, these overlapping experiences allow people to maintain a relationship with the place. preserving urban identity is not simply about retaining physical fabric but about sustaining the conditions that allow places to remain meaningful, adaptable and lived.

items.title: interpretative capacities of built-form
items.sub: b.arch design thesis · school of environment and architecture
items.description: a landscape of unusual objects: an analysis of public space identifying built-form characteristics that enable strong associations and multiple interpretations, resulting in a design proposal at the juhu selfie point sited between formal and informal settlement.
body: three public spaces were studied through the built-form characteristics that shape how people associate with and interpret their surroundings. the research identified how recognisable forms, spatial relationships and opportunities for interpretation can influence the way a place is experienced leading to a design proposal titled: a landscape of unusual objects.

the intervention sits between the juhu selfie point and an informal settlement, a transactional space used by people with different needs, routines, and relationships to the site. the brief emerged from these everyday conditions, bringing together existing necessities and aspirations rather than imposing a singular programme onto the site.

the proposal developed a landscape of objects acting as an interface between the natural landscape and the built form of the city. rather than defining a single use for each space, the objects were conceived as anchors for different activities, creating opportunities for interpretation, interaction, and appropriation. the programme brought together exhibition, play, events, learning, and quieter spaces alongside the organisational facilities required by the surrounding communities.

each object was developed through the combination of elements that symbolised a particular activity, with their scale, configuration, and relationship to one another allowing them to be read in different ways. intuitive illustrations became a starting point for developing these spatial narratives, which were then translated into built form, landscape, and circulation. ancillary spaces connect the objects into a continuous environment, while variations in enclosure, seating, level, and access allow the same space to support different modes of occupation. the resulting landscape gives physical form to the research finding that recognisable spatial cues can anchor associations while leaving room for individual interpretation.

items.title: shifting spaces: courtyard housing typology
items.description: a participatory exploration of a courtyard housing at dinghaiqiao lu in shanghai, examines how residents use and perceive shared space through observational fieldwork and a participatory spatial game. a modular intervention proposal translated these insights into flexible spaces for individual and collective activities within the compact settlement.
body: dinghaiqiao lu is a settlement organised around large courtyard spaces. despite the potential of these shared spaces, the neighbourhood is relatively introverted and disconnected from its surroundings. the study looked at how residents experienced this spatial structure and what kinds of shared spaces could better support everyday life.

site observations and conversations with residents were translated into a physical wooden block model of the settlement, using tiles to map observations, experiences and activities. the model became a game that residents could play and rearrange, creating a more direct way to understand how they perceived their neighbourhood and what kinds of spaces they wanted to see within it.

the findings informed a system of multifunctional modules designed for the compact conditions of the settlement. rather than assigning each space a fixed use, the modules could accommodate individual activities or be brought together for larger gatherings, allowing the spatial configuration to shift with changing needs and patterns of use.
